documents.unit: Office of the Provost and Executive VP for Academic Affairs
documents.title: Use of Artificial Intelligence (AI) in Academic Contexts
documents.summary: University-wide Georgia Southern policy aligned with BOR Policy 6.28. It leaves each faculty member free to decide AI use in a course but requires a syllabus AI statement, and it sets student accountability, data-protection and tool-vetting rules plus research and training provisions.
documents.stance_why: The policy sets no single student stance: 'faculty are free to use, not use, or otherwise structure the use of AI within their courses as they see fit', while requiring each instructor to write a syllabus statement, so the decision is handed to instructors (delegates).

units.why: The purpose sentence sets the university-wide frame, 'responsible, ethical, and transparent use of Artificial Intelligence (AI) tools', across teaching, research and administration, so it is a framework statement (P56) and informs rather than binds.
units.anchor: responsible, ethical, and transparent use of Artificial Intelligence (AI) tools

units.why: The scope sentence says 'All students, faculty, and staff must be aware of and comply with this policy', defining who the policy binds, which is scope (P61) rather than a rule about AI use itself.
units.anchor: All students, faculty, and staff must be aware of and comply with this policy.
units.frag_start: All students, faculty, and staff must

units.why: The statement 'recognizes the importance of critically and responsibly integrating appropriate AI technologies' welcomes AI in teaching, so it is a pro-AI default (P02); it informs because it is a recognition, not a command.
units.anchor: critically and responsibly integrating appropriate AI technologies to strengthen teaching, individualize learning

units.why: 'Research ... involving the use of AI, is encouraged' and faculty 'must adhere to the requirements of their disciplines, funding agencies, and publishers', which defers AI research rules to outside venues (P62).
units.anchor: faculty must adhere to the requirements of their disciplines, funding agencies, and publishers

units.why: 'The University maintains an inventory of permitted AI tools' is an institutional set-up fact about vetted tools, matching P50 (prefer vetted tools) as the nearest type.
units.anchor: The University maintains an inventory of permitted AI tools when using institutional and/or student data.

units.why: 'Institutional, student, or otherwise restricted data must not be entered or used in public AI tools' forbids a data use for all users, so P50 (protect personal data), restrict, must-not.
units.anchor: must not be entered or used in public AI tools.
units.frag_start: Institutional, student, or otherwise restricted data

units.why: 'Training on risks, compliance, and acceptable and ethical use of AI is a component of the required yearly training for all faculty, staff, and students' mandates training; no type covers required training, so UNCOVERED.
units.anchor: required yearly training for all faculty, staff, and students
units.uncovered_note: Required AI training for faculty, staff and students (compliance training, not faculty-support workshops).

units.why: 'The University maintains an AI Academic Governance Committee, which reviews and implements this policy ... and makes recommendations on policy updates' sets a review body, so P54 (revisit regularly).
units.anchor: AI Academic Governance Committee, which reviews and implements this policy across the University

units.why: 'Concerns about inappropriate use of generative AI should be addressed using existing processes' sends AI misuse to the Faculty Handbook and Student Code of Conduct, i.e. integrity processes (P36).
units.anchor: Concerns about inappropriate use of generative AI should be addressed using existing processes

units.why: The definition 'all members of the Georgia Southern community are responsible for the content of their work, even if aspects of it are generated by AI' makes everyone own AI-assisted output (P29).
units.anchor: responsible for the content of their work, even if aspects of it

units.why: The definition of agentive AI as a system that 'can act independently to achieve goals' sets what the policy covers, so P61 (definitions); the agent rule itself is coded separately.
units.anchor: A type of generative AI in which the system can act independently to achieve goals

units.why: The Committee is 'charged with reviewing this policy at least yearly' and checking the standard Statement Builder language, a fixed review cycle, so P54.
units.anchor: reviewing this policy at least yearly, coordinating and assisting units with the implementation

units.why: Defines AI-generated content as 'created by AI models instead of humans', fixing the policy's terms, so P61.
units.anchor: which is created by AI models instead of humans.

units.why: Defines algorithmic bias as outputs that 'may favor or discriminate against certain groups', a bias concern named in the policy, so P53.
units.anchor: AI outputs that may favor or discriminate against certain groups or concepts

units.why: Defines the term AI itself ('technology that enables computer systems to perform complex tasks normally done by humans'), which sets scope: P61.
units.anchor: technology that enables computer systems to perform complex tasks normally done by humans

units.why: Defines confirmation bias as users selectively accepting AI output, a named risk of AI use, so P53 (bias) rather than P31.
units.anchor: selectively accept outputs that align with their preexisting beliefs

units.why: 'Keep internal records of AI approvals, audits, and compliance activities' with Institutional Research maintaining records is an administrative duty; no type covers compliance recordkeeping, so UNCOVERED.
units.anchor: Keep internal records of AI approvals, audits, and compliance activities
units.uncovered_note: Institutional recordkeeping of AI approvals, audits and compliance activities.

units.why: Defines hallucinations as output that is 'plausible sounding but is incorrect, nonsensical, or fabricated', which is the P31 point that AI output can be wrong.
units.anchor: plausible sounding but is incorrect, nonsensical, or fabricated

units.why: The Flexible AI Statement Builder lets faculty 'select the language that reflects their decisions regarding the use of AI in the course' with legal-approved options, a syllabus-statement tool (P09).
units.anchor: select the language that reflects their decisions regarding the use of AI

units.why: Defines Generative AI as a subset of AI that creates content including code, setting scope: P61.
units.anchor: Generative AI is a subset of AI that creates added content

units.why: Defines Human Oversight as mechanisms by which humans 'monitor, review, and potentially intervene' in AI systems; a definition, so P61.
units.anchor: The mechanisms and processes by which humans monitor, review, and potentially intervene

units.why: Names 'Process Tracking Software' such as Turnitin Clarity, Codio and CodeGrade used to demonstrate process of writing code; process evidence tools match P40.
units.anchor: a platform to demonstrate the process of developing papers, writing code

units.why: Defines Public AI Tools as those 'not included in the University's inventory of permitted AI tools', setting the line for data rules: P61.
units.anchor: AI tools not included in the University's inventory of permitted AI tools.

units.why: Defines the Syllabus Statement as information 'outlining specific requirements and expectations for a course', a term used in the syllabus mandate: P61.
units.anchor: Information provided to students outlining specific requirements and expectations for a course

units.why: Defines transparency as AI 'developed and used in a way that allows appropriate traceability and explainability', a principle for the framework (P56).
units.anchor: allows appropriate traceability and explainability

units.why: 'The Chief Information Officer (CIO) shall establish a mechanism for procurement, review, and inventory of all AI tools' is institutional vendor review (P65), written as a duty of an admin office.
units.anchor: shall establish a mechanism for procurement, review, and inventory of all AI tools

units.why: The review 'will ensure all AI tools (regardless of cost incurred) contain provisions for addressing ethical considerations and include safeguards against bias, hallucinations, and prompt injections', a vendor-review standard (P65), with bias concern secondary.
units.anchor: include safeguards against bias, hallucinations, and prompt injections

units.why: All AI tools in the university environment 'must be documented in an institutional inventory' listing vendor, data storage and data interaction: a tool-vetting requirement (P65).
units.anchor: must be documented in an institutional inventory
units.frag_start: Al AI tools used in the

units.why: Users wanting a new tool 'must complete the Third Party Risk Review ... before purchase and/or use', which keeps tools vetted (P50) and binds any user.
units.anchor: must complete the Third Party Risk Review for risk assessment and approval

units.why: 'All tools shall be reviewed at least annually' sets a recurring review of approved AI tools; it is vendor review (P65), not a policy review (P54).
units.anchor: All tools shall be reviewed at least annually.

units.why: 'faculty are free to use, not use, or otherwise structure the use of AI within their courses as they see fit' leaves the stance to the instructor: P04 and delegates.
units.anchor: faculty are free to use, not use, or otherwise structure the use of AI

units.why: 'Faculty expectations should be communicated in clear, consistent language in an enforceable syllabus statement' asks instructors to communicate rules in the syllabus: P09.
units.anchor: Faculty expectations should be communicated in clear, consistent language in an enforceable syllabus statement.

units.why: 'each faculty member must create an AI syllabus statement' is a mandatory syllabus AI statement: P09.
units.anchor: each faculty member must create an AI syllabus statement

units.why: The statement must provide 'a working definition of AI as it relates to the course', a definition requirement for the syllabus, so P61 (definition) over P09 since the rule is about defining AI.
units.anchor: Provides a working definition of AI as it relates to the course context and policy.

units.why: The statement must give 'specific guidance ... about forbidden, restricted, and permitted AI uses' per activity, which sorts uses into categories: P05 rather than P09.
units.anchor: specific guidance to students about forbidden, restricted, and permitted AI uses

units.why: Statements must outline 'expectations for transparency, including citations of how and to what level AI was incorporated', so instructors must set a disclosure rule: P24.
units.anchor: citations of how and to what level AI was incorporated into the process

units.why: Statements must establish 'requirements for using process tracking software' and tell students of 'language detection tools, proctoring tools, process analytic tools', i.e. tools used to find misuse: P40.
units.anchor: communicates the possible use of tools to address unethical usage of AI

units.why: Statements must identify 'potential consequences for violation of these policies', which means stating penalties in advance: P37.
units.anchor: Identifies potential consequences for violation of these policies

units.why: 'Faculty are encouraged to use the Flexible AI Statement Builder tool' recommends the statement tool for consistent language, under P09.
units.anchor: Faculty are encouraged to use the Flexible AI Statement Builder tool

units.why: 'Faculty should use AI tools that have been licensed by the University' limits faculty to licensed tools to protect student data: P50.
units.anchor: Faculty should use AI tools that have been licensed by the University

units.why: 'Faculty must ensure compliance with FERPA in the handling of student work, intellectual property, and student data' is a privacy duty for faculty: P50.
units.anchor: Faculty must ensure compliance with FERPA in the handling of student work

units.why: 'Only University-approved AI tools may be used for assessing student work' limits instructor tool choice when grading; since it is about which tools are vetted, P50 and not P46 (who assigns grades).
units.anchor: Only University-approved AI tools may be used for assessing student work.

units.why: 'Faculty should inform students of their use of AI for this purpose' tells instructors to disclose their AI use in assessing student work: P47.
units.anchor: Faculty should inform students of their use of AI for this purpose.

units.why: 'Students are accountable for their use of AI as detailed in the University's Academic Dishonesty Policy' ties student AI use to the integrity code: P36.
units.anchor: Students are accountable for their use of AI as detailed in the University's

units.why: 'Any use of AI to generate content that is submitted as one's work without faculty permission and/or proper attribution is considered plagiarism' classifies unauthorized AI as misconduct: P36.
units.anchor: without faculty permission and/or proper attribution is considered plagiarism

units.why: 'Use of agentive AI to complete assessments without human interaction is considered cheating' targets autonomous agents; P07 covers agents and is where a reader would look, rather than P36.
units.anchor: Use of agentive AI to complete assessments without human interaction is considered cheating.

units.why: Students 'must complete the required AI training provided by the University', a training duty that no type covers: UNCOVERED.
units.anchor: Complete the required AI training provided by the University.
units.uncovered_note: Required AI training for faculty, staff and students (compliance training, not faculty-support workshops).

units.why: Students must 'Follow AI guidelines specified in each course', so each course sets its own rule: P04.
units.anchor: Follow AI guidelines specified in each course

units.why: Students must 'request clarification if they are uncertain about any policies', i.e. ask when unsure: P10.
units.anchor: request clarification if they are uncertain about any policies

units.why: Students must 'Maintain understanding of university-wide policies regarding the use of AI', keeping them aware of the institutional framework: P56.
units.anchor: Maintain understanding of university-wide policies regarding the use of AI.

units.why: Students must 'Follow faculty guidance on disclosure and citation of AI assistance', a disclosure duty: P24.
units.anchor: Follow faculty guidance on disclosure and citation of AI assistance

units.why: Students must 'Practice human verification and critical evaluation of AI-generated content', a verification duty: P31.
units.anchor: Practice human verification and critical evaluation of AI-generated content

units.why: 'students remain fully responsible for all submitted work, regardless of the level of AI assistance' makes students own what they submit: P29.
units.anchor: students remain fully responsible for all submitted work, regardless of the level of AI assistance

units.why: Students must 'Recognize that over-reliance on AI may undermine learning objectives and the development of critical thinking skills', a rationale that AI shortcuts skill building: P41.
units.anchor: over-reliance on AI may undermine learning objectives and the development of critical thinking skills

units.why: Students must support 'academic integrity in all coursework, including the use of AI' to preserve the credential's value; a principle statement (P56).
units.anchor: maintaining and supporting academic integrity in all coursework, including the use of AI.

units.why: 'Employees should use AI tools that have been licensed by the University' directs staff to vetted tools: P50.
units.anchor: Employees should use AI tools that have been licensed by the University

units.why: 'Student and University-specific information must not be entered or used in public AI tools' is a data prohibition for staff: P50.
units.anchor: Student and University-specific information must not be entered or used in public AI tools.

units.why: 'Users must use only authorized and anonymized data to train or interact with public AI systems', a data-protection limit: P50.
units.anchor: Users must use only authorized and anonymized data to train or interact with public AI

units.why: 'All AI-generated content must be reviewed by an employee before using it' and facts verified before reliance: a verification duty for staff, P31.
units.anchor: All AI-generated content must be reviewed by an employee before using it.

units.why: 'Staff must complete training in the ethical use of AI in the workplace' is a training duty with no matching type: UNCOVERED.
units.anchor: Staff must complete training in the ethical use of AI in the workplace
units.uncovered_note: Required AI training for faculty, staff and students (compliance training, not faculty-support workshops).

units.why: 'The University requires training to ensure faculty, staff, and students are well-equipped to engage with AI in a responsible, ethical, and informed manner' repeats the training mandate in section E: UNCOVERED.
units.anchor: The University requires training to ensure faculty, staff, and students are well-equipped
units.uncovered_note: Required AI training for faculty, staff and students (compliance training, not faculty-support workshops).

units.why: Commits that adopted AI tools 'uphold the highest standards of ethical integrity' and align with the mission; an institutional principles statement: P56.
units.anchor: uphold the highest standards of ethical integrity

units.why: 'AI tools must be evaluated for potential biases in their design, training data, and outputs' names bias as an ethical concern in tool adoption: P53.
units.anchor: AI tools must be evaluated for potential biases in their design, training data, and outputs.

units.why: Vendors 'must provide transparent documentation of how their tools function, what data they rely on' is a requirement in vendor review: P65.
units.anchor: Vendors must provide transparent documentation of how their tools function

units.why: Tools known to 'generate false or misleading information' will 'undergo additional scrutiny or may be disallowed', a vendor-screening rule: P65.
units.anchor: will undergo additional scrutiny or may be disallowed

units.why: 'AI should support, not replace, human judgment' states that AI must not replace human thinking: P32.
units.anchor: AI should support, not replace, human judgment.

units.why: 'AI tools must be accessible to all users, including those with disabilities' is an access requirement: P51.
units.anchor: AI tools must be accessible to all users, including those with disabilities.

units.why: Systems 'must be assessed for vulnerabilities, including susceptibility to prompt injection attacks', a security review of tools: P65.
units.anchor: Systems must be assessed for vulnerabilities, including susceptibility to prompt injection attacks

units.why: 'AI users must take appropriate steps to protect data and sensitive information' and treat unsecured public AI like posting publicly: P50.
units.anchor: feeding data into unsecured public AI models is potentially the same as posting it

units.why: 'Data classified as Confidential (Class 1) or Sensitive (Class 2) ... should only be provided to AI models that are listed in the approved inventory', preferring vetted tools: P50.
units.anchor: only be provided to AI models that are listed in the approved inventory

units.why: 'Academic Affairs will lead professional development opportunities for faculty and staff focused on ethical AI use, effective integration into teaching and research', supporting faculty learning: P63.
units.anchor: Academic Affairs will lead professional development opportunities for faculty and staff

units.why: 'Students will have access to additional educational programs designed to build their understanding of AI tools, promote responsible usage' offers student AI education; P63 is faculty-only, so UNCOVERED.
units.anchor: Students will have access to additional educational programs designed to build their understanding
units.uncovered_note: University-provided AI education programs for students (not faculty support).

units.why: Researchers 'are required to stay informed about emerging AI tools and evolving best practices', a research-scope duty: P62.
units.anchor: required to stay informed about emerging AI tools and evolving best practices

units.why: Researchers 'must not' enter confidential, human-subject, export-controlled or other restricted data into public AI tools: a research data prohibition, P50.
units.anchor: The following types of data must not be entered into public AI tools

units.why: 'Researchers are responsible for independently verifying the accuracy and reliability of AI-generated content': a verification duty, P31.
units.anchor: Researchers are responsible for independently verifying the accuracy and reliability of AI-generated content

units.why: 'Researchers should take steps to identify and mitigate known issues of bias in AI-generated outputs': bias concern, P53.
units.anchor: identify and mitigate known issues of bias in AI-generated outputs

units.why: 'Researchers are responsible for obtaining Institutional Review Board (IRB) approval' and the IRB reviews AI tools used with participant data: research governance, P62.
units.anchor: that AI tool is considered engaged in human subject's research, and the IRB will review

units.why: Researchers must 'Disclose the use of AI in the project and IRB application', a research disclosure duty; P62 chosen because it is addressed to IRB research, not coursework disclosure.
units.anchor: Disclose the use of AI in the project and IRB application

units.why: Researchers must 'Review and understand the Terms of Use and Privacy Policy of the software' before using it with participants, matching terms-of-use (P52).
units.anchor: Review and understand the Terms of Use and Privacy Policy of the software
units.frag_end: third party products used in research data collection

units.why: Researchers must 'Utilize AI models that are listed in the approved inventory or seek ITS approval before use with non-public data': vetted tools, P50.
units.anchor: Utilize AI models that are listed in the approved inventory or seek ITS approval

units.why: 'University members must inform themselves and comply with journal and funding agency policies regarding the use of AI' defers to external venue rules: P62.
units.anchor: must inform themselves and comply with journal and funding agency policies

units.why: Minimum documentation requires 'Name the AI tool used, its specific version, and the date range', the tool and date details of a citation: P25.
units.anchor: Name the AI tool used, its specific version, and the date range

units.why: Documentation should 'Detail how the AI tool was used ... and the extent of AI's contribution', a disclosure of purpose and extent: P24.
units.anchor: Detail how the AI tool was used

units.why: Documentation should 'Confirm that only approved AI tools were used with confidential, sensitive, restricted, or personal identifiable information': P50.
units.anchor: Confirm that only approved AI tools were used with confidential, sensitive, restricted

units.why: Documentation should show 'Evidence of human oversight of the process and review of all AI output', a verification duty: P31.
units.anchor: Evidence of human oversight of the process and review of all AI output.

units.why: Documentation 'may' include 'the specific prompts or queries provided to the AI system' or a link to chat logs, which is the prompt and log element: P25.
units.anchor: Consider including the specific prompts or queries provided to the AI system.

units.why: Documentation should 'explicitly affirm human responsibility and accountability for the final content': P29.
units.anchor: explicitly affirm human responsibility and accountability for the final content

units.why: External collaborators and AI-tool developers 'should follow the guidelines set forth above', extending research rules to partners: P62.
units.anchor: engaging with external collaborators using AI tools should follow the guidelines

units.why: 'the supervising faculty member' must ensure students and postdocs 'complete the required training and are aware of and comply with this policy', a training oversight duty: UNCOVERED.
units.anchor: supervising faculty member to ensure that their students and post-doctoral fellows complete the required training
units.uncovered_note: Required AI training for faculty, staff and students (compliance training, not faculty-support workshops).

units.why: 'The Office of the Provost will address issues related to the use of AI in the classroom' names who to contact, an institutional-framework item: P56.
units.anchor: will address issues related to the use of AI in the classroom.

units.why: 'The Office of Student Conduct will serve as the point of contact for all questions related to the Academic Dishonesty policy and use of AI' routes AI cases to integrity processes: P36.
units.anchor: Office of Student Conduct will serve as the point of contact

documents.title: Academic Affairs Policies record 51 (abstract page)
documents.summary: Abstract page for the same Georgia Southern policy; it gives only the purpose statement and compliance with BOR Policy 6.28.
documents.stance_why: The page states only that the policy gives guidance 'while encouraging innovation, academic freedom, and appropriate autonomy' and sets no stance, so it carries the delegates stance of the full policy.

units.why: The repository abstract repeats the purpose sentence of the policy, 'responsible, ethical, and transparent use of Artificial Intelligence (AI) tools', a framework statement (P56) that informs.
units.anchor: responsible, ethical, and transparent use of Artificial Intelligence (AI) tools

units.why: 'while encouraging innovation, academic freedom, and appropriate autonomy' signals support for AI innovation and instructor freedom, so P04 (instructor sets the rule) as the nearest type; it informs.
units.anchor: encouraging innovation, academic freedom, and appropriate autonomy

notes: Section G is formatted as a research documentation standard. Training mandates (faculty, staff, students, supervisors) had no matching type and are coded UNCOVERED. No school or computing-unit document was collected.
